content.text: {"title":"One Request Through Flask: What the Framework Promises Between `environ` and `200 OK`","premise":"A ten-line application — `app = Flask(__name__)`, one route returning `\"Hello, World!\"` — is the smallest thing anyone can be asked to sign off on. Nothing is configured: no secret key, no error handlers, no blueprints, no before/after hooks. Everything that happens between the client's `GET /` and the `200 OK` it gets back is Flask's own behaviour, running on its defaults. This story follows one WSGI environ dict from the moment the test client builds it to the moment the response iterator closes, and asks at each step: what is guaranteed here, what are the defaults, and what happens when something goes wrong.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"The World Before the Request: What `Flask(__name__)` Decides For You","trace_lines":[2,60],"data_in":"`import_name='__main__'`, with every other constructor argument left at its default (`static_folder='static'`, `host_matching=False`, `subdomain_matching=False`, `instance_relative_config=False`).","data_out":"A `Flask` instance carrying a `Config` of 29 defaults (`DEBUG=False`, `SECRET_KEY=None`, `TESTING=False`, `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS=None`, `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS=True`, …), a `url_map` holding two rules — `/static/<path:filename>` → `static` and `/` → `hello` — and `_got_first_request = False`.","code":["src/flask/app.py:311-364","src/flask/sansio/app.py:279-408","src/flask/sansio/app.py:479-493","src/flask/sansio/app.py:604-661","src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py:42-49","src/flask/sansio/scaffold.py:343-373","src/flask/config.py:94-100"],"inputs":["import_name='__main__'"],"characters":["Flask.__init__","App.__init__","Scaffold.__init__","App.make_config","Config","App.add_url_rule","setupmethod","Scaffold.route","get_debug_flag"],"facts":["`App.make_config` copies `Flask.default_config` and then overwrites `DEBUG` with `get_debug_flag()`, which reads the `FLASK_DEBUG` environment variable; here it returned `False` (trace line 19-20), so debug mode is off and is driven by the environment, not by code.","`SECRET_KEY` defaults to `None` and nothing in this app sets it — a fact that decides the behaviour of sessions later.","A static route is registered unconditionally whenever `static_folder` is set, without checking that the directory exists (`src/flask/app.py:352-364`); the view is held through a `weakref.ref` to the app to avoid a reference cycle (#3761).","`add_url_rule` defaults the methods to `('GET',)` and, because `PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS` is `True` and `OPTIONS` is not in the declared methods, adds `OPTIONS` to the rule and sets `provide_automatic_options = True` on it.","Every registration method is wrapped by `setupmethod`, which calls `_check_setup_finished` first; while `_got_first_request` is `False` the check passes silently (trace lines 38-40, 52-54)."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q1.1","question":"`SECRET_KEY` is `None` and no one complained. What does that mean for the session when a real request arrives?"},{"id":"q1.2","question":"`_check_setup_finished` let both registrations through. What is it actually guarding, and when does it start refusing?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":2,"title":"The Request Is Manufactured: `environ` Takes Shape","trace_lines":[61,73],"data_in":"`client.get(\"/\")` — positional args `('/',)` and `kwargs={'method': 'GET'}`.","data_out":"A `Request` object wrapping a WSGI environ: `{'HTTP_HOST': 'localhost', 'HTTP_USER_AGENT': 'Werkzeug/3.1.9', 'PATH_INFO': '/', 'QUERY_STRING': '', 'REMOTE_ADDR': '127.0.0.1', …}`.","code":["src/flask/app.py:758-814","src/flask/testing.py:125-133","src/flask/testing.py:185-202","src/flask/testing.py:204-247","src/flask/testing.py:49-86"],"inputs":["'/'","method='GET'"],"characters":["Flask.test_client","FlaskClient","FlaskClient._copy_environ","FlaskClient._request_from_builder_args","EnvironBuilder"],"facts":["`FlaskClient.__init__` seeds `environ_base` with `REMOTE_ADDR='127.0.0.1'` and a Werkzeug `HTTP_USER_AGENT`; every request the client makes inherits those (trace lines 62-70).","Flask's `EnvironBuilder` fills the host from `SERVER_NAME` or falls back to the literal `'localhost'`, and the scheme from `PREFERRED_URL_SCHEME` (`'http'` by default) — so the test request's `Host` header is a Flask config decision, not the caller's.","`FlaskClient.open` closes `self._context_stack` before dispatching, so contexts preserved by a previous request are not carried across requests or redirects.","`preserve_context` is only set inside a `with client:` block; here it is `False`, so `werkzeug.debug.preserve_context` is never added to the environ — which matters for whether the context survives the request."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q2.1","question":"The environ's `Host` is whatever the caller sent. Does Flask trust it when deciding which route matches?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":3,"title":"Crossing the Boundary: `wsgi_app` and the Context That Wraps Everything","trace_lines":[74,83],"data_in":"The environ dict plus a `start_response` callable, arriving at `Flask.__call__`.","data_out":"`<AppContext 4557234128 of scenario, GET 'http://localhost/'>` — a context holding the app, a fresh `g`, the `Request`, and a bound `MapAdapter`; not yet pushed.","code":["src/flask/app.py:1621-1628","src/flask/app.py:1569-1619","src/flask/app.py:1504-1518","src/flask/ctx.py:339-348","src/flask/ctx.py:300-337","src/flask/app.py:510-561"],"inputs":["environ","start_response"],"characters":["Flask.__call__","Flask.wsgi_app","Flask.request_context","AppContext.from_environ","AppContext.__init__","Flask.create_url_adapter"],"facts":["`__call__` delegates to `wsgi_app` purely so middleware can wrap `app.wsgi_app` without losing the app object (`src/flask/app.py:1621-1628`).","`create_url_adapter` sets `request.trusted_hosts` from the `TRUSTED_HOSTS` config and then recomputes `request.host` via `get_host(environ, trusted_hosts)`; `TRUSTED_HOSTS` defaults to `None`, meaning every `Host` header is accepted and a `SecurityError` (400) is only possible if the owner opts in.","Because `subdomain_matching` is `False`, `create_url_adapter` forces `subdomain` to the map's default (the empty string), so a request to `foo.localhost` would still match app-level routes.","`AppContext.__init__` catches an `HTTPException` raised while binding the URL adapter and stores it on `request.routing_exception` instead of letting it escape — binding failures become a normal response, not a crash.","The whole of `push()` + `full_dispatch_request` sits inside a `try/except Exception` in `wsgi_app`, with `ctx.pop(error)` in a `finally`: the context is popped even on unhandled errors."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q3.1","question":"If anything inside dispatch raises an exception that no handler claims, what does the client actually see?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q2.1","answer":"Yes — `create_url_adapter` recomputes `request.host` from the environ, and with the default `TRUSTED_HOSTS = None` no host is rejected. Host validation is opt-in config, not a built-in guarantee."}]},{"n":4,"title":"Push: The Session Opens Before the URL Is Matched","trace_lines":[84,101],"data_in":"The unpushed `AppContext` holding the `Request` and `MapAdapter`.","data_out":"The active context: `_cv_app` set, `_session = <NullSession {}>`, and `request.url_rule`/`request.view_args` filled in from the match on `/`.","code":["src/flask/ctx.py:416-444","src/flask/ctx.py:381-393","src/flask/sessions.py:323-335","src/flask/sessions.py:303-321","src/flask/sessions.py:150-169","src/flask/sessions.py:83-97","src/flask/ctx.py:405-414"],"inputs":["AppContext"],"characters":["AppContext.push","AppContext._get_session","SecureCookieSessionInterface.open_session","SecureCookieSessionInterface.get_signing_serializer","SessionInterface.make_null_session","NullSession","AppContext.match_request"],"facts":["`push()` is idempotent-by-count: `_push_count` is incremented every time, and if `_cv_token` is already set it returns immediately, so signals and routing fire only on the first push (`src/flask/ctx.py:428-432`).","The order is deliberate: the session is opened first, then `match_request()` runs, so custom URL converters and `open_session` implementations can see the request context (`src/flask/ctx.py:437-444`).","`get_signing_serializer` returns `None` when `app.secret_key` is falsy (trace lines 89-93); `open_session` then returns `None` and `_get_session` substitutes a `NullSession` — reads return empty, and `__setitem__`, `pop`, `update`, `setdefault` etc. all raise `RuntimeError(\"The session is unavailable because no secret key was set…\")`.","`match_request` catches `HTTPException` from `url_adapter.match()` and parks it on `request.routing_exception`; a 404 or 405 is therefore decided here but not raised here.","Routing is skipped entirely if `url_adapter is None` (no `SERVER_NAME` and no request), leaving `url_rule` unset."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q4.1","question":"A routing failure would now be sitting silently on `request.routing_exception`. Who turns it into a response?"},{"id":"q4.2","question":"This is a `NullSession` that refuses writes. Will anything still try to send a `Set-Cookie` for it?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.1","answer":"No secret key means no signing serializer, which means no real session: the context installs a `NullSession` that reads as empty and raises `RuntimeError` on any write. Session failure is loud at write time, silent at read time."}]},{"n":5,"title":"`full_dispatch_request`: The Error Boundary and the Setup Lock","trace_lines":[102,112],"data_in":"The pushed `AppContext` (`GET 'http://localhost/'`, matched endpoint `hello`).","data_out":"`None` from `preprocess_request` — no before-request hook short-circuited, so dispatch proceeds.","code":["src/flask/app.py:995-1022","src/flask/app.py:1369-1395","src/flask/wrappers.py:161-195","src/flask/sansio/app.py:410-420"],"inputs":["ctx"],"characters":["Flask.full_dispatch_request","Flask.preprocess_request","Request.blueprints","Request.blueprint","_got_first_request"],"facts":["`self._got_first_request = True` is set here, before dispatch; from this request onward every `setupmethod` (`route`, `add_url_rule`, `before_request`, `errorhandler`, …) raises `AssertionError` — late registration is refused rather than silently half-applied.","`request_started.send(...)`, `preprocess_request(ctx)` and `dispatch_request(ctx)` all run inside one `try/except Exception as e: rv = self.handle_user_exception(ctx, e)` — a failing `before_request` hook is handled exactly like a failing view.","`preprocess_request` runs URL value preprocessors for all names first, then before-request functions; any non-`None` return from a before-request function becomes the response and dispatch is skipped entirely (`src/flask/app.py:1390-1393`).","Scope order is app-first for preprocessing: `names = (None, *reversed(req.blueprints))`. Here `req.blueprints` is `[]` because the endpoint `'hello'` contains no dot (trace lines 106-111), so only app-level hooks are considered.","`full_dispatch_request` also emits a `DeprecationWarning` on the first request if `should_ignore_error` has been overridden — a deprecated hook scheduled for removal in Flask 3.3."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q5.1","question":"The view is about to return a plain Python string. What makes that a valid HTTP response, and what happens if a view returns something Flask can't interpret?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.2","answer":"`_check_setup_finished` guards against registering routes or hooks after the app has begun serving. The lock engages right here, at the top of `full_dispatch_request`, when `_got_first_request` flips to `True`."}]},{"n":6,"title":"`dispatch_request`: The Three Branches, Two Not Taken","trace_lines":[113,118],"data_in":"The pushed `AppContext` with `request.url_rule` pointing at the `/` rule and `view_args = {}`.","data_out":"`'Hello, World!'` — the raw return value of the view function.","code":["src/flask/app.py:969-993","src/flask/app.py:563-589","src/flask/app.py:1056-1066","src/flask/app.py:1068-1103"],"inputs":["ctx"],"characters":["Flask.dispatch_request","Flask.raise_routing_exception","Flask.make_default_options_response","Flask.ensure_sync"],"facts":["The first branch checks `req.routing_exception is not None` and calls `raise_routing_exception`, which re-raises the stored exception — so a 404 parked during `match_request` surfaces here, inside the error boundary, and becomes a normal error response.","`raise_routing_exception` only substitutes a debug-only `FormDataRoutingRedirect` when debug mode is on, the exception is a `RequestRedirect` with a code other than 307/308, and the method is not GET/HEAD/OPTIONS; with `DEBUG=False` the original exception is always re-raised unchanged.","The second branch returns `make_default_options_response(ctx)` when the matched rule has `provide_automatic_options` and the method is `OPTIONS`; that rule flag was set during registration in Chapter 1. Here the method is `GET`, so the branch is skipped.","`ensure_sync` inspects the view with `iscoroutinefunction`; a plain `def` is returned unchanged (trace lines 116-117). An `async def` view would go through `async_to_sync`, which raises `RuntimeError(\"Install Flask with the 'async' extra…\")` if `asgiref` is missing.","The view is called as `self.ensure_sync(self.view_functions[rule.endpoint])(**view_args)` — the endpoint-to-function mapping, not the rule, decides what runs."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q4.1","answer":"`dispatch_request` does, as its very first act: `raise_routing_exception(req)` re-raises the stored `HTTPException` inside `full_dispatch_request`'s `try`, where `handle_user_exception` converts it into a response."}]},{"n":7,"title":"`make_response`: Turning a `str` Into a `Response`, or Refusing To","trace_lines":[119,121],"data_in":"`rv = 'Hello, World!'` (a bare `str`), handed to `finalize_request`.","data_out":"`<Response 13 bytes [200 OK]>`.","code":["src/flask/app.py:1024-1054","src/flask/app.py:1227-1367"],"inputs":["rv='Hello, World!'"],"characters":["Flask.finalize_request","Flask.make_response","Response"],"facts":["Tuple returns are unpacked first: a 3-tuple is `(body, status, headers)`, a 2-tuple is disambiguated by whether the second item is a `Headers`/`dict`/`tuple`/`list`; any other length raises `TypeError` with an explicit message about the allowed forms.","Returning `None` (or falling off the end of a view) raises `TypeError` naming the endpoint — it is never silently turned into an empty 200.","`str`, `bytes`, `bytearray` and iterators are passed to `response_class` directly so the class can apply status and headers itself; `dict` and `list` go through `self.json.response(...)`; a `BaseResponse` or any callable is coerced via `response_class.force_type` as a WSGI app; anything else raises `TypeError` listing the valid return types.","`DefaultJSONProvider.response` uses compact separators out of debug mode and 2-space indentation in debug mode, and `sort_keys`/`ensure_ascii` default to `True` — JSON output shape depends on `DEBUG`.","`finalize_request` wraps `process_response` and the `request_finished` signal in a `try`; failures only get swallowed (and logged) when `from_error_handler=True`, which is set only by `handle_exception` — in the normal path a failing `after_request` propagates."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q5.1","answer":"`make_response` normalizes the view's return value, creating a `Response` from the `str` body. Unsupported return types — `None`, odd-length tuples, arbitrary objects — raise `TypeError` with a message naming the allowed forms, so misuse fails loudly rather than producing a broken response."}]},{"n":8,"title":"`process_response`: After-Request Hooks and the Cookie That Isn't Written","trace_lines":[122,137],"data_in":"`<Response 13 bytes [200 OK]>` plus the active `AppContext`.","data_out":"The same `<Response 13 bytes [200 OK]>`, unmodified, with no `Set-Cookie` and no `Vary` header.","code":["src/flask/app.py:1397-1421","src/flask/ctx.py:118-148","src/flask/sessions.py:162-169","src/flask/sessions.py:337-385"],"inputs":["response","ctx"],"characters":["Flask.process_response","ctx._after_request_functions","SessionInterface.is_null_session","SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session"],"facts":["Per-request callbacks registered with `after_this_request` run first, then registered `after_request` functions; blueprint scopes run before the app scope (`chain(ctx.request.blueprints, (None,))`) and within each scope in reverse registration order — the inverse of `preprocess_request`'s ordering.","Each after-request function must return a response; its return value replaces `response` for the next function, so a hook that forgets to return breaks the chain.","`save_session` is called only when `is_null_session(ctx._get_session())` is `False`. Here the session is a `NullSession`, so the call is skipped entirely (trace lines 131-134) and no cookie is written.","When a real session is in play, `save_session` adds `Vary: Cookie` whenever `session.accessed` is true, deletes the cookie if the session was emptied and modified, and otherwise only sets it if `should_set_cookie` — modified, or permanent with `SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST`.","Cookie defaults are conservative-but-not-strict: `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True`, but `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=False`, `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=None`, `SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED=False` — secure/SameSite hardening is the owner's job."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q4.2","answer":"No. `process_response` checks `is_null_session` and skips `save_session` entirely, so a secret-key-less app sends no session cookie and no `Vary: Cookie` header."}]},{"n":9,"title":"`pop`: Teardown That Runs Everything, Even When It Fails","trace_lines":[138,187],"data_in":"The active `AppContext` and `exc=None` (no error occurred during dispatch).","data_out":"`None` — context popped, `_cv_app` reset, `_cv_token = None`, request closed, no errors collected.","code":["src/flask/ctx.py:446-504","src/flask/app.py:1423-1454","src/flask/app.py:1456-1482","src/flask/helpers.py:654-682"],"inputs":["ctx","exc=None"],"characters":["AppContext.pop","_CollectErrors","Flask.do_teardown_request","Flask.do_teardown_appcontext","Request.close","appcontext_popped"],"facts":["`pop` refuses to run against the wrong context: it raises `RuntimeError` if `_cv_token` is `None`, if no context is active, or if the active context is not `self` — mismatched push/pop is a hard error, not corruption.","`_push_count` is decremented and cleanup is skipped while it is still positive, so a context pushed N times (streaming, `stream_with_context`, test preservation) only tears down on the Nth pop.","Every teardown step runs inside a `_CollectErrors` block whose `__exit__` records the exception and returns `True` (swallowing it); `raise_any` then raises a `BaseExceptionGroup` on Python ≥3.11 (or the first error otherwise). Guarantee: one failing teardown callback does not prevent the others, `request.close()`, or the contextvar reset from running (trace lines 139-187).","Teardown order is fixed: request teardowns (blueprint scopes then app, reverse registration order) → `request_tearing_down` signal → `request.close()` → appcontext teardowns reversed → `appcontext_tearing_down` → reset `_cv_app` → `appcontext_popped`.","`exc` is forwarded to every teardown function; if an error handler already produced a response, `wsgi_app` passes `error=e` only for exceptions that escaped `full_dispatch_request`, so handled errors are not seen by teardown."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[]},{"n":10,"title":"Out the Door: The Response Iterator, and the Path Not Taken","trace_lines":[188,190],"data_in":"`<Response 13 bytes [200 OK]>` called as a WSGI app with `(environ, start_response)`.","data_out":"`<werkzeug.wsgi.ClosingIterator object at 0x10fa1ef90>`, surfacing to the caller as `<WrapperTestResponse streamed [200 OK]>` with body `'Hello, World!'`.","code":["src/flask/app.py:1595-1619","src/flask/app.py:900-951","src/flask/app.py:868-898","src/flask/app.py:833-866","src/flask/app.py:953-967"],"inputs":["environ","start_response"],"characters":["Flask.wsgi_app","Flask.handle_exception","Flask.handle_user_exception","Flask.handle_http_exception","Flask.log_exception","got_request_exception"],"facts":["`return response(environ, start_response)` happens inside the `try`, so the `finally` — and therefore `ctx.pop(error)` — runs before the body is iterated by the server; the response is already materialized by then.","Had the view raised, `handle_user_exception` would look up a handler by status code and MRO across blueprint then app scope; `HTTPException`s go to `handle_http_exception` unless `trap_http_exception` says otherwise. With no handler registered for a non-HTTP exception it re-raises, falling through to `handle_exception`.","`handle_exception` always sends `got_request_exception`, then checks `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS`; it defaults to `None`, which resolves to `self.testing or self.debug`. In this app both are `False`, so the exception would be logged via `log_exception` and the client would get a generic 500 `InternalServerError` with the original error attached as `original_exception` — the traceback is never sent to the client unless debug or testing is on.","The 500 path still goes through `finalize_request(..., from_error_handler=True)`, so `after_request` functions and session saving run even for the default 500 response, and failures there are logged instead of raised.","The `finally` block also restores the context for the Werkzeug debugger when `werkzeug.debug.preserve_context` is in the environ, and clears `error` when the deprecated `should_ignore_error` hook claims it — both inactive here."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[{"id":"q3.1","answer":"An exception that escapes dispatch is caught by `wsgi_app`, sent to `handle_exception`, announced on `got_request_exception`, and — because `PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` resolves to `testing or debug`, both `False` here — logged server-side and returned to the client as a generic 500. Flip `TESTING` or `DEBUG` on and the same exception is re-raised instead."}]}]}
